title: Evaluation of a Sustainable Capillary Electrophoresis Method for Drug Monitoring
author: Othman, Weam M.
materials: Comparison of the proposed CE-PDA with reported methods.

steps.title: Prepare calibration and QC samples (spiked plasma)
steps.instruction: Construct two series of test tubes containing NIL and OFL at concentrations ranging from 0.5 to 80 µg mL⁻¹ in rat plasma; for each tube add 100 µL of the SAR internal‑standard working solution (0.5 mg mL⁻¹) and bring the total volume to 1 mL with the background electrolyte (BGE). Prepare QC tubes at 20, 40 and 60 µg mL⁻¹ for both analytes using the same procedure.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards with protein precipitation
steps.instruction: In separate test tubes transfer NIL and OFL amounts to obtain 0.5–80 µg mL⁻¹ from their 0.5 mg mL⁻¹ working solutions; add 200 µL blank rat plasma and 100 µL internal‑standard solution (0.5 mg mL⁻¹), vortex 1 min, then add acetonitrile to bring the volume to 1 mL, vortex another 1 min, and centrifuge at 5 000 rpm (~2 830 × g) for 10 min to precipitate proteins.

steps.title: Store QC samples at –20 °C
steps.instruction: After preparation, place all QC tubes (20, 40, 60 µg mL⁻¹ for NIL and OFL) in a –20 °C freezer until analysis.

steps.title: Inject samples into CE‑PDA instrument
steps.instruction: Inject each calibration and QC sample in triplicate into the capillary electrophoresis system equipped with a photodiode array detector under the previously optimized electrophoretic conditions; record peak‑area ratios of analyte to internal standard.

steps.title: Generate calibration curves and assess linearity
steps.instruction: Using the triplicate injections, plot peak‑area ratios versus nominal concentrations (0.5–80 µg mL⁻¹) for NIL and OFL, perform ordinary‑least‑squares regression, and obtain linear equations, correlation coefficients (r = 0.9998 for NIL, 0.9996 for OFL), slopes (1.891 for NIL, 1.960 for OFL) and intercepts (‑1.3915, ‑2.784). Determine LOD (0.12 µg mL⁻¹ NIL, 0.13 µg mL⁻¹ OFL) and LLOQ (0.30 µg mL⁻¹ NIL, 0.40 µg mL⁻¹ OFL) based on a 3:1 signal‑to‑noise ratio and acceptable accuracy/precision, incorporating the 5‑fold dilution factor used during sample preparation.

steps.title: Assess method specificity
steps.instruction: Run electropherograms for (a) blank plasma, (b) plasma spiked with NIL, OFL and internal standard, and (c) plasma from rats dosed with NIL + OFL and spiked with internal standard; confirm absence of interfering peaks at the migration times of the three analytes.

steps.title: Evaluate accuracy and precision
steps.instruction: Perform intra‑day (same day) and inter‑day (different days) assessments by analyzing five replicates of each QC level (20, 40, 60 µg mL⁻¹) for both drugs; calculate bias % [(measured‑nominal)/nominal × 100] and relative standard deviation (RSD%). Expected intra‑day bias: –4.69 % to 3.11 %; inter‑day bias: –3.21 % to 2.87 %; intra‑day RSD: 1.66 %–4.25 %; inter‑day RSD: 1.26 %–5.34 %, all within FDA criteria.

steps.title: Test sample stability
steps.instruction: Subject QC samples at the three concentration levels to (a) bench‑top stability at 25 °C for 6 h and (b) three freeze‑thaw cycles (‑20 °C for 12 h, then thaw to room temperature); after each condition re‑inject and calculate recoveries. Observed recoveries: NIL 96.48 % ± 3.29 % to 105.47 % ± 3.14 %; OFL 96.28 % ± 2.11 % to 102.39 % ± 2.43 % (n = 5).

steps.title: Determine extraction recovery
steps.instruction: Compare peak areas of extracted plasma samples (prepared as above) with those of pure standard solutions; calculate mean recoveries of 101.36 % ± 1.84 % (SD) for NIL and 99.99 % ± 2.01 % (SD) for OFL (n = 3).
